notes.text: A portrait handwritten leaf on listing paper. The authorial number 1 is at the top centre; a separate lower-left 33 is preserved as unassigned foliation. No date is written on this leaf. H’s opening editorial account is not manuscript text.

The page defines special five-point systems (Sigma,K) by the existence of a nontrivial automorphism and announces a classification by the automorphism group. This definition is transcribed, not independently established.

The live finite-order sentence says that every finite-order automorphism of Sigma has exactly two fixed points. Taken literally this includes the identity, so it requires a nontriviality qualification; the earlier g≠1 lies in cancelled text. The identity counterexample was checked, and no qualification was inserted into the transcription.

Conditional on the page’s stated two-fixed-point bound and free nonfixed-orbit premise for the nontrivial g, write 5=a+b nu with 0≤a≤2 and b≥1. This yields 2≤nu≤5 and fixed-point counts 0,1,2 for nu=5,4,3 respectively. Reader B checked the bound and enumerated the integer possibilities; this is not an independent proof of the fixed-point premise.

For nu=5 the manuscript gives the orbit mu_5(k), the double-struck D_5 inside a loop open at the upper-left, and uniqueness up to isomorphism, with a pentagonal structure. The group identification and categorical assertion were transcribed but not independently proved.

For nu=4 the live revised equation is K^g={P}; the canceled equation has plain initial K without a separate raised g, and capital Card. The complement is one orbit, the pole remains infinity|0, and the full group is Z/4Z ≃ mu_4(k). The category is compared with oriented squares. The orbit count was checked under C03; the full group and categorical assertions were not separately proved.

For nu=3 the page gives Card K^g=2, inserts K^g=Sigma^g and =J, and identifies the remaining orbit with mu_3. It compares the category with combinatorial triangles/Ens(3), associates Sigma_J and poles to J, and writes D_3. The orbit count was checked under C03; the categorical construction and automorphism group were not independently proved.

Clear serif I is retained in permutation de I, the complements I minus {P} and I minus K^g, and the pentagon margin. The omega argument favors I but now explicitly admits J because of its returning foot. K and J occur elsewhere; none is silently regularized from the construction.

The first margin has a roof spanning G_m and the wording est celle|usuelle. The crossed order-5 prefix favors forall while nu remains possible. The case3 canceled letter retains Sigma|K with an additional doubtful low2 index. Letter and cancellation extent after Sigma_J remain unresolved, as do the pole symbol, raised g cluster, field-letter case, and the opening Partition|Une partition. The later margin phrase is richesse en symétries.

The replacement qu’on peut supposer mu_3 is written below the crossed Le groupe total est|des auto. The curved leader from Card K^g=2 to the inserted donc clause is not set as a parenthesis. The comma belongs inside that insertion; est une orbite remains live.
Root independently checked the same orbit arithmetic, conditional on the page’s stated two-fixed-point and free-orbit premises. This confirms the counts for nu=5,4,3 without emending any I/K letters.

Root personally viewed all48 differing fixed crops and completed second/148_scan034_root_working.json before implementation. The operation, pentagon and partition margins were also viewed after rotation of the full saved crops by50 degrees clockwise. Root reopened the existing complete case3_est, association and ending evidence crops where fixed boxes clipped relevant letter parts. No new image judgment was made by the mechanical implementer. The eight literal matches were not reopened. The first, second, boxes, comparison and token-difference TSVs are preserved byte for byte.

The first sphere keeps its original .75 scale and receives the approved angular rear mark and separate short vertical. The second sphere uses native crop coordinates with x=.0075cm and y=-.00818cm; the third uses x=.00706cm and y=-.0080cm. Both use the explicit root-specified physical line widths and point radii. The inline D5 loop uses x=.007cm and y=-.007cm, a .5pt open path and the same double-struck label. Clip commands, overlapping text and specified neighboring strokes are omitted. No TeX compilation was performed.

Three new C/H rows record capital Card in the definition, the case3 fixed-count formula and de Card3. The canceled case2 Card is included in its existing complete-equation row. The additional canceled low2 is included in the existing canceled-symbol row. New alternatives, narrowed doubts, the inserted-comma wrapper and coordinate changes alone receive no additional C/H row. The canceled case2 K and the canceled symbol after Sigma_J have no source MARKS IDs among the nine scan034 entries; their existing doubts and C/H rows are updated without inventing identifiers. Existing mathematical checks are unchanged.
